summary: This is a GitLab CI job configuration that sets up SSH authentication to connect to a self-hosted GitLab server. It installs SSH tools, decodes a stored private key, registers it with the SSH agent, and verifies the connection works by attempting an SSH login.

explanations.4: The pipe character (|) means the following indented lines are treated as a single shell script block that runs together.
explanations.5: This installs the SSH client and Git tools needed for authentication, using the -y flag to auto-answer yes to prompts.
explanations.6: ssh-agent is a background process that holds your SSH key in memory so you don't need to type your password repeatedly; the eval command activates it in this shell session.
explanations.7: This creates the .ssh directory if it doesn't exist and restricts its permissions to just the owner (700), which is required by SSH for security.
explanations.9: The SSH_PRIVATE_KEY variable contains your private key in base64 (encoded) format, so this decodes it and saves it as the file SSH will look for.
explanations.13: ssh-keyscan connects to the GitLab server and retrieves its public host key, then appends it to known_hosts so SSH knows it's a trusted server and won't prompt you to verify it.
explanations.16: This comment explains the test: we're verifying SSH authentication works by connecting to GitLab and requesting server info (the -T flag means no command execution, just test the connection).
